# nonEmpty

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** empty.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonEmpty() — Checks whether a value is **not** empty. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.1.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonEmpty(value: unknown): boolean;
```

`nonEmpty(value)` is the same test as `!isEmpty(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Emptiness is read per kind: `null` and `undefined`, a string with nothing but whitespace, an array, `Set` or `Map` with no entries, an object with no own keys. `0` and `false` are values, not emptiness.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not empty; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonEmpty(0); // => true
nonEmpty(false); // => true
nonEmpty("a"); // => true
nonEmpty([0]); // => true
nonEmpty(null); // => false
nonEmpty(""); // => false
nonEmpty("   "); // => false
nonEmpty([]); // => false
nonEmpty({}); // => false
nonEmpty(new Map()); // => false
```
